rewrites.summary:
This division stands under the national framework as it operates across all the country's regions. Same-sex activity is not criminalised, but the 2023 laws ban same-sex marriage and legal gender transition, trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, and no discrimination legislation based on sexual orientation or gender identity covers housing, healthcare or employment.

Enforcement exposure is documented and severe: 'gay propaganda' offences carry fines up to 400,000 roubles (about £3,600) for individuals or up to 15 days' detention, repeat offences can bring criminal prosecution with up to four years in prison, and the November 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement makes participation punishable by 2-6 years and organising by 6-10 years. Between December 2022 and March 2024 at least 139 people were affected by enforcement of anti-LGBT+ laws, 101 'extremism'-related convictions (98 administrative, three criminal) were recorded since the designation took force in January 2024, and the official assessment is that trans people and publicly active LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. The audited sources document no division-specific pattern, so the national risk profile governs what a visitor encounters here.

A foreign-government travel advisory advises against all travel regardless of personal characteristic because of wrongful-detention and arbitrary-law-enforcement risk.

The official assessment treats trans people, publicly active LGBT+ advocates and the conflict-affected region cluster as likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. A foreign-government travel advisory notes that official support is 'very limited' in parts of the country. National support groups report emigration, asylum requests and the closure of queer spaces accelerating after the designation. The audited sources document no division-specific pattern, so national conditions govern what a visitor encounters here.
